content.text: Rational ethics asks for **consistency**. If an act is wrong in one case, it is wrong in any case exactly like it, unless some relevant difference sets them apart.

content.definition: Making the same judgment about cases that are alike in every relevant way, whoever is involved.

examples.title: Cutting in line
lines: I say it is fine for me to cut in line because I am in a hurry.
Would I accept everyone in a hurry cutting in front of me?
examples.note: If not, my principle fails the consistency test.

examples.title: Lying
lines: It is wrong for you to lie to me.
It is fine for me to lie to you.
examples.note: Inconsistent, unless I can name a relevant difference between the two cases.

question.prompt: What does consistency in ethics require?
question.hint: Think about two cases that differ only in who is involved.
question.explanation: Consistency means making the same judgment about cases that are alike in every relevant way.
